messages.subject: Re: Contingency table question
messages.body_plain:
for the chi-squared, you can select "conservative" and monte-carlo,
and that will give you the level alpha p-value. You can't do that for
the fisher's exact test, but you can change it in the command line
with the conservative=TRUE option:

tables<-add.fishers.exact(tables,conservative=TRUE)

ian

messages.subject: Re: Data viewer of deducer - viewing data.frames which have vector elements
messages.subject_clean: Data viewer of deducer - viewing data.frames which have vector elements
messages.body_plain:
It would make some sense to add functionality for alternate object
types such as survival times, but not matrices. It is pretty bad
practice to put lists or matrices in data.frames.

Ian

For every row of the data frame, i would like to make some calculations (same calculation for every row). I would like to break down these calculations into steps and i would like to get intermediate outputs between these steps (intermediate outputs are vectors). So i write a function for each step. I then apply() the function to the rows of the data frame and add a column to the data frame with the result of the function. This way i get to observe the intermediate outputs.
